[[File:Noether.jpg|thumb|Emmy Noether before 1910]]
[[Emmy Noether]] (1882–1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra. This article is dedicated to the things named after her achievements.

==Mathematics==
{{columns-list|colwidth=15em|
* [[Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether theorem]]
* [[Primary decomposition|Lasker–Noether theorem]]
* [[Noether identities]]
* [[Noether normalization lemma]]
* Noether's bound
* [[Isomorphism theorems|Noether's isomorphism theorems]]
* [[Rational variety#Rationality questions|Noether’s problem]]
* [[Noether's second theorem]]
* [[Noether's theorem]]
* [[Conserved_current|Noether Current]]
* [[Noether's theorem|Noether Charge]]
* [[Skolem–Noether theorem]]
}}

==="Noetherian"===
* [[Noetherian]]
* [[Noetherian group]]
* [[Noetherian induction]]
* [[Noetherian module]]
* [[Noetherian ring]]
* [[Noetherian scheme]]
* [[Noetherian topological space]]

==Other==
{{columns-list|colwidth=20em|
* "Noether boys",  nickname for [[Emmy Noether#Graduate students|her doctoral students]]. 
* [[Noether Lecture]] held every year, by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Citation | chapter-url = http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Introduction.html | chapter = Introduction | title = Profiles of Women in Mathematics | series = The Emmy Noether Lectures | publisher = [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] | year = 2005 | accessdate = 13 April 2008 | archive-date = 23 May 2011 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110523234115/http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Introduction.html | url-status = dead }}.</ref>
* ''Emmy Noether Campus'', the building used by [[University of Siegen]] to house its mathematics and physics departments.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://www.uni-siegen.de/uni/campus/wegweiser/emmy.html | title = Emmy-Noether-Campus | publisher = Universität Siegen | place = [[Germany|DE]] | accessdate = 13 April 2008}}.</ref>
* ''Emmy Noether Programme'', operated by the German Research Foundation ([[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]]).<ref>[https://www.dfg.de/en/research-funding/funding-opportunities/programmes/individual/emmy-noether "Emmy Noether Programme: In Brief"]. ''Research Funding''. [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft]]. n.d. Retrieved on 23 March 2025.</ref>
* A street in her hometown, [[Erlangen]], has been named after Emmy Noether and her father, [[Max Noether]].
* A street in Moosach, North-West [[Munich]], has been named after her.
* ''Emmy Noether School'', in Erlangen.<ref name = "g_noether_p167">{{Harvnb | Noether | 1987 | p = 167}}.</ref>
* Emmy Noether High School Mathematics Days, series of high school workshops and competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.ttu.edu/~enoether/|title=Emmy Noether Highschool Mathematics Day|website=www.math.ttu.edu|access-date=2016-03-30|archive-date=2020-07-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731003647/http://www.math.ttu.edu/~enoether/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Emmy Noether Visiting Fellowships, at the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/emmy-noether-visiting-fellowships|title=Emmy Noether Visiting Fellowships - Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=2016-03-30|archive-date=2017-10-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029071505/http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/emmy-noether-visiting-fellowships|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* LMS [[Emmy Noether Fellowship]]s, at the [[London Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/grants/lms-emmy-noether-fellowships|title=LMS Emmy Noether Fellowships
|website=lms.ac.uk}}</ref>
* The Emmy Noether Council, also at the Perimeter Institute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/support-pi/emmy-noether-council|title=Emmy Noether Council|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326073955/http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/support-pi/emmy-noether-council|archivedate=2015-03-26}}</ref>
* The Emmy Noether Mathematics Institute in the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, [[Bar-Ilan University]], Ramat Gan, Israel - jointly founded by the university, the [[German government]] and the [[Minerva Foundation]]. 
* The Emmy Noether lectures (an annual series of distinguished lectures).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~eni/|title=Emmy Noether Research Institute for Mathematics|website=u.cs.biu.ac.il|access-date=2016-03-30|archive-date=2020-01-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200105094440/http://u.cs.biu.ac.il/~eni/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Emmy Nutter, the (fictional) physics professor in "The God Patent" by [[Ransom Stephens]], is based on Emmy Noether.<ref>{{Citation | url = http://ransomstephens.com/the-god-patent.htm | title = The God Patent | first = Ransom | last = Stephens | access-date = 2016-03-30 | archive-date = 2014-08-02 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140802054737/http://www.ransomstephens.com/the-god-patent.htm | url-status = dead }}.</ref>
}}

===Astronomy===
[[File:Far side 21.jpg|thumb|Part of the [[USGS]] far side lunar chart]]

* The crater [[Nöther (crater)|Nöther]] on the [[far side of the Moon]] is named after her.
* The [[7001 Noether]] asteroid also is named for her.{{Sfn |Schmadel|2003| p= 570}}<ref>Blue, Jennifer. [https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/ Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature]. [[United States Geological Survey|USGS]]. 25 July 2007. Retrieved on 13 April 2008.</ref>
